payload.title: Tue 12/1: Referring providers: progress notes as requested
payload.purpose: What a referring provider can ask for during the program, and how the registered nurse coordinates care.

captions.LI: Referring providers can request progress notes at any time during a patient's enrollment in the Bariatric Counseling Center program. Our registered nurse coordinates care with referring medical providers to ensure continuity with any current treatment plans patients may have. At patient discharge, we give referring providers a detailed summary of the patient's behavioral progress during the time in our intensive outpatient program, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression, among other metrics. The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medications that patients receive from their medical providers. We accept most health insurances. Our claims are processed under patients' mental health benefits. The Bariatric Counseling Center serves patients in San Antonio and virtual across Texas. #BehavioralHealth

payload.purpose: Saturday 10:00 to 1:00 for people whose week has no room.

Our Saturday track runs from 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., available both onsite and virtually. It's the same comprehensive program, behavioral therapy and counseling, dietary guidance and support, culinary classes, and mindful movement. One program, not four.

For professionals managing demanding schedules, this track offers a path to sustainable progress without compromising your weekday commitments. The Bariatric Counseling Center serves clients in San Antonio and virtual across Texas, and the program is in-network with most health insurance plans.

If Saturday mornings work better than weekday sessions, we're here.

#BehavioralHealth

payload.title: Mon 12/14: Coping skills that are not food
payload.purpose: Recovery & Coping Skills: three ideas from the program for the hard hour of the day.

captions.FB:
When the hard hour hits, food doesn't have to be the answer.

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we teach Recovery & Coping Skills as part of our Behavioral Therapy & Counseling pillar. Here are three ideas from the program:

Name the feeling. Sometimes just saying it out loud takes the edge off. Angry, lonely, tired. You don't have to fix it right away. You just have to know what it is.

Move your body for five minutes. Not to burn anything off. Just to shift the energy. A walk around the block. Stretching in your living room. Movement can break the loop.

Call someone who gets it. Not to solve it. Just to hear a voice that reminds you that you're not alone in this.

These are small tools, but they add up. We teach them in group and individual therapy, alongside dietary guidance, cooking classes and movement education. One program, not four.

Bariatric Counseling Center. San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

payload.title: Tue 12/15: Referring providers: who is the right referral
payload.purpose: Standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or alongside bariatric surgery or weight loss medication. Pre and post bariatric patients in one bullet.

captions.LI: The Bariatric Counseling Center serves patients at every stage of their weight management journey. Our intensive outpatient program provides standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or works alongside bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers. We support pre-surgical patients preparing for bariatric procedures, post-surgical patients navigating recovery, and patients on weight loss medications who need comprehensive behavioral support. The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. Healthcare professionals in four disciplines. One program, not four. Our team coordinates care with referring medical providers and, at patient discharge, we give referring providers a detailed summary of the patient's behavioral progress during the time in our intensive outpatient program, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression, among other metrics. Progress notes as requested, typically within two business days. We accept most health insurances; our claims are processed under patients' mental health benefits. San Antonio and virtual across Texas. Our Director of Admissions is Leloni Gonzales at lgonzales@bccsanantonio.com and 210-634-2200. #BehavioralHealth
